Thanks for the details, Maya — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups and a short POC outline so you know what to expect in the deep-dive: 

Quick technical notes on noisy-neighbor risk and options:
- Hosted (shared) — good for low-risk prototypes. We mitigate cross-tenant interference via continuous batching, token-weighted fair scheduling, and prefix KV caches; however, absolute isolation at the host level isn't guaranteed, so tail latency can be affected by noisy workloads.
- Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools (node-level isolation) with tenant-only scheduling. Good tradeoff for predictability and lower unit cost than full Private deployments.
- Private VPC / On-prem — full network and host isolation, KMS-sourced keys inside your VPC, audit logs forwarded to your SIEM. Recommended for PHI/EU-residency workloads.

Suggested POC (48–72 hrs):
1) Baseline capture: mirror a sample of production traffic (anonymized) to a dedicated test pool (no downstream user impact). Capture token distributions, latencies, and cache-hit rates.
2) Stress windows: inject synthetic bursts up to your peak (120 qps) to observe 95/99p latency behavior under load.
3) Isolation experiment: compare a small Dedicated pool vs shared-host baseline. Measure tail variance and KV cache warmup.

What we need from your side before the deep-dive:
- A short sample trace (CSV/JSON) showing request timestamps, token counts, and payload sizes (can be anonymized).
- Confirmation on whether you need HSM-backed KMS or if cloud KMS is fine.
- Any IP allowlist or egress rules if we provision a Private VPC test.

Attachment: redwood-poc-plan.md (POC checklist and test cases)

If the 5/4 10:00 PDT slot works, I can run through the test plan and preliminary sizing (how many GPUs to reserve for the POC).
